item.title: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case is Bundibugyo strain
item.description: The first Ebola case detected in Nigeria is the Bundibugyo strain and the patient is a diplomat, an emergency meeting to discuss the outbreak was told on Wednesday. “We did three levels of tests, but all molecular. The strain was Bundibugyo,” Olajumoke Babatunde, director public health lab service at the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention said, referring to the same strain of the virus behind the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. “This person is actually a diplomat,” another official said adding the patient has deteriorated into “multi organ failure”. item.title: Ebola: Kano govt activates emergency operatiions centre
item.description: The Kano State Centre for Disease Control (KNCDC) has activated a Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC), following the Federal Government’s announcement of an Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). This is contained in a public advisory by the centre’s Director-General, Prof. Muhammad Adamu-Abbas, in Kano on Tuesday. Adamu-Abbas said the centre is fully ready and on high alert for any eventualities. “The Federal Government confirmed one case of imported Ebola in Abuja. The patient is already isolated and receiving care. Forty-four people who had close contact with the patient have been found and are being monitored every day. “Here in Kano, the KNCDC Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) is on high alert. There is no need to panic, but we must all be careful and act quickly,” the Director-General said. He called on residents to be calm while cautioning them to also abide by mandatory protocols to avoid the occurrence of the outbreak or further spread of the disease. He listed the mandatory protocols to include not going to a pharmacy, chemist, or local drug shop to self-medicate and not boarding public transportation (buses, taxis, keke, or Adaidaita) to minimise exposing others, while individuals who came down with the infection must be immediately isolated in a private room. He said the signs and symptoms of ebola could include sudden high fever, extreme weakness, severe headache, body and joint pains, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, and unexplained bleeding. “Ebola infection occurs if the blood or body fluid of an infected person touches the eyes, nose, mouth or a wound on the skin. It can also be contracted through touching clothes, bedding or surfaces that have a sick person’s fluid. “For prevention, wash your hands always with soap and running water for at least 20 seconds. Do not touch sick people or their belongings. Do not touch dead bodies. “Do not eat bushmeat. If you must eat meat, buy from clean markets and cook it very well. Clean your house, especially door handles, phones and tables with disinfectant or bleach. “If you have a fever and any of the danger signs and you have travelled or met someone who is sick, do not go to a chemist or stay at home. “Call health officials immediately on KNCDC 07077974504, kanocdc@gmail.com, or kano_cde on Facebook, X, or Instagram, or call your LGA Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer (DSNO), or report to any health facility. In a related development, the director-general also advised all public, private, faith-based and military facilities in the state to be on the look out. He also directed them to ensure strict compliance with the Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) while warning them against compromise on IPC enforcement to protect the patients and the health workers. item.title: The Opposition Has A Numbers Problem. Tinubu Has A Trust Problem
item.description: Nigeria’s presidential election is less than three months away, and something rather curious is happening. The ruling party is gathering supporters from almost every political direction. The opposition is gathering presidential candidates who cannot quite agree on who should lead them. And the electorate is being asked to choose between an administration defending difficult economic reforms and challengers promising a different future. There is plenty of political activity. What remains less clear is whether there is enough political persuasion. This Tuesday, three developments help explain where the race is heading: growing divisions within the opposition, a new controversy over the security of a presidential candidate, and an increasingly uncomfortable argument about who should bear the cost of Nigeria’s economic reforms. Together, they point to a contest that may ultimately be decided not by the size of political rallies, but by the credibility of the choices placed before Nigerians. 1. Atiku’s supporters can argue that he has national networks, experience and an established electoral base. But there is an uncomfortable truth for all three camps. Votes are not bags of rice that politicians can simply transfer from one warehouse to another. A coalition agreement signed in Abuja does not guarantee that voters in Kano, Onitsha, Ibadan or Port Harcourt will follow the instructions of their preferred politicians. And the longer these negotiations continue, the less time remains for building the trust, campaign organisation and common policy programme needed to make a joint ticket credible. The APC will be watching with considerable interest. Every week spent arguing about who should lead the opposition is a week the ruling party can spend campaigning. 2. Wike’s Rainbow Coalition meets resistance Wike (L) There is another coalition attracting attention, but this one is working in the President’s favour. Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike has been promoting what he calls a Rainbow Coalition to support Tinubu’s re-election. The idea is politically attractive to the APC: recruit influential figures from other parties without necessarily requiring them to abandon their existing political platforms. But today’s reports suggest the arrangement is encountering resistance within the PDP. Party officials in Oyo, Imo, Edo and Bauchi, among other states, have distanced themselves from the initiative. Some insist that their party will continue to support its own candidates rather than subordinate its interests to Tinubu’s campaign. This matters for two reasons. First, it suggests that Wike’s political influence, although substantial, is not unlimited. Second, it raises an intriguing question about the future of party loyalty in Nigeria: Can a politician campaign for the presidential candidate of another party while remaining committed to his own party’s electoral success elsewhere? The answer may depend on political circumstances, but the implications go beyond Wike. If parties become vehicles for personal arrangements rather than institutions built around programmes and principles, the distinction between government and opposition becomes increasingly difficult for voters to understand. Tinubu may benefit from these arrangements in the short term. But the larger question is whether such alliances strengthen democratic competition or simply make it harder for citizens to identify who stands for what. 3. A dangerous allegation enters the campaign Atiku (centre) Today’s most troubling political development concerns an allegation about the safety of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. Timi Frank, a member of the ADC and former APC official, has alleged that there is a plot to assassinate the opposition presidential candidate. The APC Presidential Campaign Council has strongly denied the allegation. Its spokesperson, Dele Alake, challenged Frank to provide evidence and urged security agencies to investigate any credible threat. The council also stated that President Tinubu had directed security agencies to strengthen protection for candidates. There is no independently established evidence in the reporting reviewed that substantiates the alleged plot. Nevertheless, the development deserves attention. An election campaign should be a contest of ideas, personalities and political programmes, not an atmosphere in which threats and accusations dominate public discussion. If there is credible evidence of a threat, it must be investigated promptly and impartially. If an allegation is unfounded, that too should be established. Neither side should exploit such a serious matter for political advantage. The responsibility of the authorities is to ensure that every candidate can campaign freely and safely. That is not a favour to the opposition. It is a fundamental obligation of democratic government. 4. The economy returns to the centre of the campaign Organised labour has demanded a minimum wage review. Away from the coalition negotiations, another political confrontation is developing. The Nigeria Labour Congress has maintained its two-week ultimatum to the Federal Government, demanding renewed wage negotiations amid rising petrol prices and continued pressure on household incomes. Labour argues that the ₦70,000 minimum wage is no longer sufficient to meet basic living expenses. President Tinubu, meanwhile, has again defended the removal of petrol subsidies, insisting that he has no regrets about the decision. This is becoming one of the defining arguments of the 2027 election. The government says subsidy removal was necessary to correct longstanding economic distortions, reduce fiscal pressures and create the foundation for sustainable growth. item.title: Australian Lawmaker Loses Legs After ‘Targeted’ Attack
item.description: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has had both legs removed after what police called a “targeted” attack. item.title: France braces for more protests – security measures at a glance
item.description: After a weekend of protests, riots and looting, France is looking to head off further unrest, ahead of fresh demonstrations called for Saturday. Here are some of the measures authorities have ordered: – Curfews – Partial nighttime curfews were imposed in parts of Paris and several other cities on Monday and Tuesday nights, applied to areas where clashes broke out last weekend and shopping zones that had been targeted by looters. Paris also banned public gatherings on the Champs Elysees, near major public buildings, and near train stations. Marseille, France’s second-biggest city, has banned unaccompanied minors from central shopping streets every night up to and including Friday. – Bans – Paris police have banned people carrying bottles or cans of petrol or gas, or possessing fireworks, up to and including Thursday. Last weekend, youths set fire to several shops and public buildings, and shot fireworks through tubes at police, wounding several. – Deployment – French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has vowed a “massive” security deployment for Saturday, after his government admitted it “lost control” last weekend. President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday said authorities would be “uncompromising” towards “agitators from ultra-left fringe groups” that he blamed for much of the violence. Elite police units have been mobilised for the coming weekend. Macron has not, however, declared a state of emergency that would allow troops to be sent to reinforce police lines. However, soldiers who for more than a decade have been patrolling sensitive sites, airports and train stations and tourist zones under “Operation Sentinelle” would continue to be deployed to protect those spots. – Shops – The government has announced interest-free loans for 3,000 shops that were damaged, many of them looted, during last weekend’s unrest. Shop owners say that is not enough, though. Crowdfunding initiatives have sprung up on social media for residents to help their local shops rebuild. But the total amount being raised is only in the low hundreds of thousands of euros — whereas the sector says the damage bill will run to hundreds of millions. – Burnt bikes – Tourists visiting Paris right now hoping to use the usually ubiquitous rental bikes available via apps might find them a bit more scarce. More than 1,000 of the 40,000 bicycles deployed across the capital were destroyed, often burned, as they were thrown into makeshift street barricades built by protesters, according to an AFP tally of figures from the operators. – Food deliveries – Staying in and ordering food delivery could also be a problem for some. The Union-Independants union covering most delivery bike riders has asked Uber Eats, Deliveroo and other such companies to suspend deliveries to areas considered dangerous. It called for the riders to be able to cancel deliveries without losing money and for them to have a system allowing them to see risky areas in real time. item.title: Student loans voluntary, not compulsory, NELFUND tells tertiary institutions
item.description: … Fund says borrowing is voluntary, urges institutions to stop misleading students By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) has declared that no student in Nigeria’s tertiary institutions is under any obligation to apply for a student loan, insisting that the scheme is designed to assist those facing financial hardship, not compel every student to borrow. The Fund, in a clarification issued on Wednesday, stressed that accessing the interest-free loan remains a personal decision that must be guided by a student’s financial circumstances and genuine need for assistance. NELFUND’s position comes amid the need to ensure that students, tertiary institutions and other stakeholders clearly understand the purpose and conditions of the federal government’s student loan initiative. The Fund explained that the scheme was established to break financial barriers to higher education and prevent eligible Nigerian students from abandoning their academic ambitions because of a lack of funds. It, however, cautioned against any interpretation or practice that could make borrowing compulsory for students, irrespective of their financial capacity. item.title: Regulator has ‘power’ to force Man city sale if charges upheld
item.description: English football’s Independent Regulator (IFR) will have “absolute power” to force Manchester City’s owners to sell if they are ultimately found to have run the club improperly, the watchdog’s chair has said. Premier League leaders City have been found guilty on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules by an independent commission between 2009 and 2018. The club have appealed and deny any wrongdoing, but face a severe sanction unless they overturn the verdict. Owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, City have blossomed into the dominant force in English football since a 2008 takeover. “We have the power to ask an owner to step away from a club if we believe that they run a club in a way that is neither fit, fair or done with propriety,” the IFR’s chair David Kogan told “The Rest is Football” podcast. Asked if an owner could refuse to divest, Kogan added: “No. We’ve got absolute power to do so.” Kogan also said last week he would resign if there is any political interference in any investigation the IFR may undertake into City. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has come under criticism for his initial comments on City’s guilty verdict, saying he would be “really concerned” if the club’s Abu Dhabi owners left the club following the verdict. Downing Street subsequently had to backtrack, insisting no one was “above the rules”. Burnham, who was mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to June 2026, has since published all of his dealings with the City hierarchy. But the case poses a delicate balancing act for the UK government in preserving its longstanding ties with the Emirates without interfering in the independence of the disciplinary action against City. item.title: Ebola: NCDC urges calm, strengthens FCT surveillance
item.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has urged Nigerians to remain calm and rely on verified information following the confirmation of an Ebola disease case in the Federal Capital Territory. The agency disclosed this in a post on its X platform on Wednesday, saying the Federal Government, through the NCDC and relevant health authorities, was strengthening surveillance and response efforts. The NCDC explained that Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person who is sick or has died, as well as contact with contaminated materials. It urged members of the public to report suspected cases promptly, stressing that early reporting was critical to saving lives. The agency advised Nigerians to seek information from credible sources and avoid spreading unverified reports about the outbreak. item.title: 2027: APC campaign council reshuffles youth, women mobilisation teams
item.description: The PBAT/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council has announced changes to its leadership structure, including the creation of a directorate to oversee stage organisation and management ahead of the general elections. Imo State Governor and council secretary, Hope Uzodimma, announced the appointments in a statement on Monday, saying the changes were designed to improve coordination, strengthen the council’s structure and boost operational efficiency. Under the new arrangement, Farouk Aliyu will head the Directorate of Stage Organisation and Management, with Adejare Bello appointed as co-director. The council also named Youth Development Minister Ayodele Olawande as director of youth mobilisation, while Dayo Israel will serve as his deputy. For women mobilisation, Mary Aille Idele was appointed director, with Betta Edu as deputy director and Imaan Suleman as secretary. Uzodimma said the appointments were part of efforts to establish a coordinated and inclusive campaign structure capable of mobilising support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. He said the appointees were expected to deploy their experience and organisational skills to their respective roles and collaborate with other directorates in implementing the council’s campaign and mobilisation plans. The changes come as the ruling All Progressives Congress prepares for the 2027 presidential election, with youth and women mobilisation identified as key components of its campaign strategy. item.title: Zamfara 2027: Governor Lawal, 14 other candidates sign peace accord
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State and 14 other governorship candidates yesterday signed a peace accord to ensure peace and order in the forthcoming 2027 General elections. The accord, organised by the Zamfara State Police Command in Gusau, was signed at the Peace Accord and Election Security Summit held in Zamfara State. The Peace Accord signing ceremony was meant to ensure peace and order for all political parties in the country as a preparation for free and fair 2027 elections. Governor Lawal, along with all contestants in the governorship, national and state assembly elections, were invited to sign and promise that no one will violate or work against any election processes before, during and after elections. The governor, as one of the contestants under the All Progressive Congress (APC), signed the accord and prayed for peace, free and fair elections, and all the political parties did the same. In his speech, Zamfara State Commissioner of Police, CP Ahmed Mohammed Bello Daga, called on all the contestants to shun, avoid, and not try to violate any election processes before, during and after elections. He warned that any political aspirant or member of any political party found violating the law will be decisively trailed and charged before the court of law. Also, the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Zamfara State Command, Kabir Abdul Randawa, has assured political parties and residents of the command’s commitment to providing adequate security and ensuring peaceful political activities in the state. He urged all political parties and candidates to shun intimidation, violence and other acts capable of threatening the peace. item.title: NMA raises alarm over doctors’ health, burnout
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu The Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), Enugu State chapter, has called for improved working conditions and greater attention to doctors’ welfare, warning that medical practitioners risk compromising their own health while caring for patients. The state Chairman of the association, Dr Ortuanya Emeka, made the call in Enugu during a press briefing to mark the 2026 Physicians’ Week celebration. Ortuanya said the theme of the celebration, “Saving the Savers — Promoting Physicians’ Well-being and Preventing Burnout, Cardiovascular Disease, and Premature Death,” highlighted the challenges confronting medical practitioners. He said the future of medicine depended not only on professional commitment but also on a healthy and motivated workforce, supportive government policies, adequate healthcare infrastructure, quality medical education and the responsible adoption of modern technology. According to him, doctors routinely work long hours, handle emergencies, make critical decisions and bear the emotional burden of human suffering, often under difficult working conditions. “Unfortunately, most times, if not at all times, we become so committed to our duties to the point of neglecting our own lives,” he said. The NMA chairman stressed that physicians’ well-being should be treated as a practical professional priority rather than an issue discussed only during ceremonial occasions. He urged Governor Peter Mbah, through the Commissioner for Health, Prof. George Ugwu, to strengthen advocacy for safe working conditions and create an environment where doctors could deliver quality healthcare without unnecessary occupational risks. “We must encourage healthcare employers and relevant authorities to recognise that an exhausted workforce cannot be expected to function indefinitely at its best,” he said. Ortuanya also condemned violence against healthcare workers, describing threats, intimidation, harassment and physical attacks on doctors as unacceptable. He said hospitals should provide safe environments for both patients and healthcare professionals, warning that insecurity in medical facilities could undermine effective healthcare delivery. “Our hospitals must be places of healing, not environments in which healthcare professionals fear for their safety,” he said. The NMA chairman further called for sustained engagement with relevant authorities to address issues affecting medical practitioners, including remuneration, career progression, workplace safety, training opportunities and the availability of essential resources. He said improving doctors’ welfare and working conditions was essential to sustaining a motivated medical workforce and ensuring quality healthcare delivery. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 21, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira maintained relative stability against the United States Dollar across both official foreign exchange windows and the parallel market in early trading on Wednesday, October 21, 2026. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the Naira opened trading exchanging at approximately N1,330.97 to N1,332.00 per US Dollar. The current spot rate reflects ongoing interventions and foreign portfolio flows sustaining liquidity within the official autonomous market window. Meanwhile, in the unofficial parallel market, street traders and Bureau De Change (BDC) operators across key commercial hubs such as Lagos and Abuja quoted buying rates around N1,365 per dollar and selling rates near N1,380 per dollar. The premium between the official window and the parallel market continues to hover around N48 to N50 per dollar as retail demand for foreign travel, international tuition payments, and non-official commercial imports remains active. At these rates, a $100 bill translates to approximately N133,097 at the official rate and up to N138,000 when purchased through parallel market channels. Market analysts note that FX liquidity conditions remain closely linked to international crude oil receipts and domestic monetary policy measures aimed at stabilising foreign capital inflows. Nigeria’s Ebola Outbreak Explained Nigeria’s experience with Ebola Nigeria’s experience with Ebola in 2014 demonstrated how quickly an imported infection could become a national public health emergency in a country with a large population and busy international travel routes. On July 20, 2014, Patrick Sawyer, a Liberian-American diplomat who was infected with Ebola, arrived at Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos from Liberia. He was subsequently admitted to a private hospital, where his illness was initially difficult to distinguish from other diseases. He died on July 25, 2014. His arrival triggered an emergency response involving the Federal Ministry of Health, the Lagos State Government, the NCDC and international health partners. According to a report published in the United States Centres for Disease Control and Prevention’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, Nigeria recorded 20 Ebola cases, comprising 19 laboratory-confirmed cases and one probable case, by September 24, 2014. Eight fatalities from seven laboratory-confirmed Ebola and one probable case were recorded. The deaths included Sawyer and Dr Ameyo Stella Adadevoh, who placed the foreigner in quarantine, as well as six others who were infected during the chain of transmission that followed his arrival. The outbreak was eventually contained, with no new cases reported after August 31, 2014. The country identified and monitored 894 contacts during the response, while 11 patients with laboratory-confirmed Ebola were discharged from care. How prepared is the country for Ebola? Nigeria’s latest preparedness efforts began before the reported FCT case. On June 9, 2026, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu approved the immediate release of N10 billion as emergency intervention funding for public health preparedness and response. The fund is separate from a N21.2 million per-state disbursement under the State Outbreak Investigation and Response Fund. The Presidency also announced the establishment of a Presidential Task Force on Ebola Virus Disease Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats, chaired by the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila. According to the State House, the fund was intended to strengthen the operational capacity of the NCDC and support critical national public health emergency response activities. The government also directed states hosting international airports and international border corridors, alongside relevant ministries, departments and agencies, to submit their preparedness plans, funding requirements and intervention needs. The measures announced included intensified passenger screening at international airports, enhanced monitoring of passengers arriving through designated high-risk routes, and the activation of referral and isolation centres at the Lagos and Abuja international airports. Other proposed measures included health declaration systems for passengers arriving from or transiting through designated high-risk countries and improved coordination among health, immigration, aviation and security authorities. The funding decision followed warnings about the possibility of Ebola being imported into Nigeria as outbreaks emerged in Central Africa. In a May 28, 2026, advisory, the NCDC assessed Nigeria’s risk of importation as high, citing regional transmission, international travel, population movement, porous land borders and the difficulty of distinguishing early Ebola symptoms from common illnesses such as malaria and Lassa fever. The agency said preparedness needed to cover every state and the FCT, with emphasis on early detection, isolation, laboratory diagnosis, infection prevention and control, contact tracing and the protection of healthcare workers. Daily Trust reported in September that three months later, there was no public breakdown of how the N10 billion was spent, as checks at airports and isolation facilities revealed the presence of the preparedness gap the money was meant to close. Several travellers, who spoke to this paper then, said they were required to provide identification and health information through an app before returning to Nigeria, but to their amazement, no checks were carried out at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, on their arrival. “They didn’t ask me for anything.
